messages:
IncidentBot: PAGE: p99 latency SLO breach detected for shared-gpu-pool-7 - streaming p99=1200ms (> SLO 400ms). Affected routes: /stream, /chat. Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:12:02Z. Auto-alerting on-call.
Jamie: Ack - I'm on channel, paging SRE. Priya, you up?
Priya: I'm oncall, looking. Pulling recent graphs and kv-cache metrics.
Ben: I see host-gpu-31 with nvme writeback spikes and blkio throttle events. One tenant process (acct-7243) doing heavy checkpointing and large writes.
Elena: Support has incoming tickets - several customers report streaming stalls and increased 502s starting ~03:10. Ticket TKT-8342 linked.
Priya: p95 is mostly stable but p99 blown out. KV cache evictions concurrent with host IO spike. Suspect noisy neighbor causing tail.
Jamie: Ok immediate plan: 1) apply per-tenant IO throttle on acct-7243 2) drain/evacuate host-gpu-31 3) enable fallback quantized model for /stream routes 4) notify affected customers. Who can apply throttle now?
Ben: I can apply cgroup/blkio limits. Planning to set max throughput to 30MB/s for acct-7243. Executing now. 
Ben: `sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.read_bps_device=8:0 31457280 acct-7243` (example). Pushing change.
IncidentBot: Deploybot: policy update applied to host-gpu-31 by Ben at 03:16 UTC.
Priya: Good - seeing immediate drop in host write latency. p99 trending down to ~480ms but still above target. KV cache still warming.
Jamie: Carlos - can you coordinate host drain/evac? We want tenants moved off host-gpu-31 and runtime restarted. ETA?
Carlos: On it. Starting drain now, migrating active sessions to standby pool. ETA ~6 minutes for full evacuation. Will restart runtime after movers complete.
Maya: CS: prepping customer comms. Elena, can you share list of impacted accounts (errors >5%) so we can prioritize outreach?
Elena: Sending short list now: acct-1289, acct-7243, acct-9910. Draft to customers: "We observed increased latency for streaming; we've applied mitigations and are routing to fallback pools. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps"
Priya: After drain, we'll likely see residual tail due to cache misses. Plan to route critical customers to fallback pool with quantized model for 15min to absorb warmup.
Ben: Enabled fallback routing: /stream now uses model q4_512 for routed traffic. Live config change applied, verifying.
Ben: p99 for routed traffic down to ~320ms. Streaming stalls reduced, errors dropping.
Jamie: Status update: throttle applied, host draining, fallback model enabled. Handoff: Priya primary investigator, Ben and Carlos supporting. I'll hold channel until SLO <400ms for 30m. Marking Sev2.
Priya: Capturing logs and perf graphs (nvme, blkio, runtime traces). Flagging acct-7243 for follow-up: recommend billing/abuse review and tighter IO caps.
Maya: Customer outreach sent to impacted list and status page updated. Some customers report degraded output quality due to fallback model change; CS collecting impact and will escalate if needed.
Carlos: Host drain complete, runtime restarted, NVMe writeback steady at baseline. No long-running IO tasks remaining.
IncidentBot: SLA Monitor: shared-gpu-pool-7 p99 = 365ms at 03:40 UTC (below threshold).
Jamie: Great. Keep monitoring for 30m. Priya put together mitigation timeline and proposed permanent guardrails: auto per-tenant IO caps, auto-evac on writeback spike, and improved cache priming for fallback.
Priya: Will produce runbook and post-incident action items: include exact cgset commands, dashboard links, alert thresholds, and owner list. I'll attach graphs and dmesg in the postmortem.
Ben: Action item for runtime: add soft limits for KV cache eviction to avoid simultaneous mass evictions after evictions/evacuations.
Elena: I'll coordinate the follow-up customer emails once root cause doc is ready.
Jamie: Thanks everyone. Closing active mitigation; leaving the channel open for postmortem notes and follow-up tasks.
